successCriteria.description: `BalanceService.initializeBalance(employeeId, leavePolicyId, fiscalYear)` reads the policy's `entitlementDays` via `ILeavePolicyRepository.findById` and creates a `LeaveBalance` via `ILeaveBalanceRepository.create` with `totalEntitlement=entitlementDays`, `usedDays=0`, `remainingDays=entitlementDays`, `status='ACTIVE'`, and the given `fiscalYear`. If the policy is not found, it throws a typed error `{ error: string; code: 'POLICY_NOT_FOUND' }`.
`BalanceService.getBalance(employeeId, leavePolicyId, fiscalYear)` delegates to `ILeaveBalanceRepository.findByEmployeeAndPolicy` and returns the result. If no balance exists, it returns `null`.
`BalanceService.getBalancesForEmployee(employeeId, fiscalYear)` delegates to `ILeaveBalanceRepository.findByEmployeeId` and returns the array of balances.

`NotificationService.notifyLeaveSubmitted(leaveRequest)` creates a `LeaveNotification` with `type='SUBMITTED'`, `status='PENDING'`, `leaveRequestId=leaveRequest.id`, and `recipientId` set to the employee's manager (resolved via `IEmployeeRepository.findById(leaveRequest.employeeId)` then `IEmployeeRepository.findById(employee.managerId)`). If the employee has no manager, the notification is still created with `recipientId` set to a sentinel or the employee themselves — the implementation must not throw.

`NotificationService.notifyLeaveApproved(leaveRequest)` and `notifyLeaveRejected(leaveRequest)` each create a `LeaveNotification` with `type='APPROVED'` or `type='REJECTED'`, `status='PENDING'`, `leaveRequestId=leaveRequest.id`, and `recipientId=leaveRequest.employeeId` (the employee who submitted the request).

`NotificationService.notifyLeaveCancelled(leaveRequest)` creates a `LeaveNotification` with `type='CANCELLED'`, `status='PENDING'`, `leaveRequestId=leaveRequest.id`, and `recipientId` set to the employee's manager (same manager-resolution logic as `notifyLeaveSubmitted`).

`NotificationService.getNotificationsForUser(recipientId)` delegates to `INotificationRepository.findByRecipientId` and returns the array. `NotificationService.markAsRead(id)` delegates to `INotificationRepository.updateStatus(id, NotificationStatus.READ)`.

Stub interface files exist at `src/modules/audit/audit.service.interface.ts` (exporting `IAuditService` with `logAction(entityType, entityId, action, oldValues, newValues, performedBy): Promise<AuditLog>`), `src/modules/leave-policy/leave-policy.service.interface.ts` (exporting `ILeavePolicyService` with `getPolicy(id)`, `getPolicyByType(leaveType)`, `isActive(id)`), and `src/modules/employee/employee.service.interface.ts` (exporting `IEmployeeService` with `getEmployee(id)`, `getManager(employeeId)`, `isActive(id)`). Each file compiles cleanly and imports only from its own module's model or shared types.

Jest unit tests exist at `tests/unit/modules/leave-balance/leave-balance.service.test.ts` and `tests/unit/modules/notification/notification.service.test.ts`. Each test file mocks the repository dependencies and verifies all service methods: correct delegation, correct parameter passing, correct error propagation, and correct notification recipient targeting (manager vs employee).

constraints: Fiscal year is calendar year (Jan 1 – Dec 31), hardcoded. The `initializeBalance` method uses the `fiscalYear` parameter as-is; no configurable fiscal-year-start logic is introduced in this phase. [BINDING RULE from reconciled.json business_rules]

All database access goes through repository interfaces (GP-001). `BalanceService` must depend on `ILeaveBalanceRepository` and `ILeavePolicyRepository`; `NotificationService` must depend on `INotificationRepository` and `IEmployeeRepository`. No direct DB calls.

Services must not import from other modules' internals — only from their barrel `index.ts` (or the module's public entry point). `BalanceService` imports from `../leave-balance` and `../leave-policy`; `NotificationService` imports from `../notification` and `../employee`.

Error semantics must match the existing contract: thrown errors are plain objects `{ error: string; code: string }`. `BalanceService.initializeBalance` must throw `{ error: 'Leave policy not found', code: 'POLICY_NOT_FOUND' }` when the policy does not exist. `NotificationService` notify methods must not throw on missing employee/manager — they should handle gracefully (e.g., skip notification or use a fallback).

The `daysRequested` BINDING formula `(endDate.getTime() - startDate.getTime()) / (1000 * 60 * 60 * 24) + 1` is NOT used in this phase — balance initialization does not compute days. The formula is already implemented in `LeaveRequestService` (Phase 8). This phase must not duplicate or redefine it.
outOfScope: Full implementations of `AuditService`, `LeavePolicyService`, and `EmployeeService` — only stub interface files are created in this phase.
DB-backed repository implementations — all repositories remain stubs that throw "not implemented".
Integration of `BalanceService` and `NotificationService` into `LeaveRequestService` — the existing `LeaveRequestService` does not call audit or notification modules; that wiring is deferred.
RBAC enforcement at the HTTP layer (GP-005) — routes accept all requests without auth guards. Manager checks remain at the service layer only.

ambiguities.description: The `initializeBalance` interface signature accepts `fiscalYear: number` as a parameter, but the PLAN.md description says "fiscalYear=current calendar year (hardcoded Jan 1 – Dec 31 per BINDING rule)." Should the implementation derive the fiscal year from `new Date().getFullYear()` (ignoring the parameter), or use the parameter as-is?
options: Use the fiscalYear parameter as-is — the caller decides the fiscal year
Ignore the parameter and always derive fiscalYear from new Date().getFullYear()
Use the parameter but validate it matches the current calendar year

entityInvariants.invariant: `remainingDays` MUST equal `totalEntitlement - usedDays` at all times. `BalanceService.initializeBalance` sets `usedDays=0` and `remainingDays=totalEntitlement`, satisfying this invariant at creation. Any future mutation to `usedDays` (in other services) must recalculate `remainingDays` accordingly.

Every `LeaveNotification` created by `NotificationService` must have `status='PENDING'` and `readAt=null` at creation time. The `type` must match the lifecycle event that triggered it (SUBMITTED, APPROVED, REJECTED, or CANCELLED). The `leaveRequestId` must reference the `LeaveRequest.id` that triggered the notification.

A `LeaveBalance` initialized via `BalanceService.initializeBalance` must have `status='ACTIVE'`. The composite uniqueness constraint `(employeeId, leavePolicyId, fiscalYear)` is enforced by the repository layer — the service must not create a duplicate balance for the same tuple.

interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Throws `{ error: 'Leave policy not found', code: 'POLICY_NOT_FOUND' }` when `ILeavePolicyRepository.findById` returns null. Throws repository-level errors unwrapped if the underlying create fails (e.g., duplicate key).

Must not throw if the employee or manager cannot be resolved. If `employee.managerId` is null, the notification should target the employee themselves or use a defined fallback — the implementation chooses the shape but must not throw.

Delegates to `INotificationRepository.updateStatus(id, NotificationStatus.READ)`. If the notification does not exist, the repository returns null — the service should propagate this as a no-op (void return) rather than throwing.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: `BalanceService` must use the same `LeaveBalance` entity shape defined in `src/modules/leave-balance/leave-balance.model.ts` — specifically the fields `totalEntitlement`, `usedDays`, `remainingDays`, `fiscalYear`, `status` with the union type `'ACTIVE' | 'EXHAUSTED' | 'CLOSED'`.

`NotificationService` must use the same `LeaveNotification` entity shape defined in `src/modules/notification/notification.model.ts` — specifically the fields `recipientId`, `type` (union of 'SUBMITTED' | 'APPROVED' | 'REJECTED' | 'CANCELLED' | 'BALANCE_LOW' | 'BALANCE_EXHAUSTED'), `title`, `message`, `leaveRequestId`, `status` (NotificationStatus enum), `readAt`.

`NotificationService` must use `IEmployeeRepository.findById` (not `IEmployeeRepository.findByManagerId`) to resolve the employee and their manager. This matches the existing pattern in `LeaveRequestService` (Phase 8) which uses `employeeRepo.findById` for manager checks.

Error objects thrown by services must match the shape `{ error: string; code: string }` used throughout `LeaveRequestService` (Phase 8). No `new Error()` throws for business-logic failures — only for truly unexpected internal errors.

The stub interface files (`IAuditService`, `ILeavePolicyService`, `IEmployeeService`) must import entity types from their respective module models: `AuditLog` from `src/modules/audit/audit.model.ts`, `LeavePolicy` from `src/modules/leave-policy/leave-policy.model.ts`, `Employee` from `src/modules/employee/employee.model.ts`. The `LeaveType` enum used in `ILeavePolicyService.getPolicyByType` must come from `src/shared/types/index.ts`.

integrationPoints.why: `BalanceService` and `IBalanceService` must be exported from the leave-balance barrel so that `LeaveRequestService` (and future modules) can import them.
`NotificationService` and `INotificationService` must be exported from the notification barrel so that `LeaveRequestService` (and future modules) can import them.
